evidence: app/package.json:5-10 — pins @angular/* ^22.2.0, the current stable major (v22.0 released 2026-06-03)
app/src/app/pages/home/home.ts:26 — resource() backs the home page's data loading; stable only since v22
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/pokemon-page.ts:29 — resource() for the core Pokémon page, plus a second chained resource at :40
app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:50 — @Service() decorator, introduced v22.1 (Apr 2026), stable in v22
app/src/app/pages/type-page.ts:86, ability-page.ts:45, move-page.ts:77, types-page.ts:27 — resource() on every remaining page
reach.rationale: No experimental or preview APIs at all, but the app's entire data layer rests on resource(), which only became stable ~5 months ago in v22, plus the equally fresh @Service decorator — squarely 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/src/app/pages/home/home.ts:26 — resource() called directly in the component, no wrapper; same pattern in 5 other page files
app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:100-140 — all fetching lives in framework-free async methods (speciesIndex, types, cardsFor), so resource() is a thin declarative shell per page
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/poves-table.ts:1 — (moves-table.ts) uses only stable signal/computed/input; no experimental API leaked into shared components
app/src/app/shared/load-state.ts:15 — loading/error UI consumes resource() state via a plain input, keeping the shared component API-agnostic
containment.rationale: Partly contained: six direct resource() call sites across all pages, but each is a one-line declaration delegating to plain async loaders in core/, so a swap touches six lines and no data logic — no dedicated wrapper though.

evidence: app/src/app/pages/pokemon/pokemon-page.ts:40-44 — second resource keyed on selectedGame() re-fetches move tables when the ?game= query param changes; params-driven reload/cancel is much simpler than an RxJS switchMap equivalent
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/pokemon-page.ts:30 — params: () => this.name() reloads on route change, replacing manual subscribe/teardown
app/src/app/shared/load-state.ts:1-15 — hasValue()/error() state consumed declaratively with zero RxJS in the whole app
app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:50-51 — @Service() is ergonomics-only over @Injectable({providedIn: 'root'}); mildly gratuitous but it is now the documented default
justification.rationale: Every resource() use buys real simplification (keyed reloads, cancellation, no observables); the single @Service() use is a style pick, stable and officially recommended, so nothing is novelty for its own sake.

findings.issue: resource(), stable only since Angular v22 (Jun 2026), is the data-loading mechanism of all six pages with no thin wrapper of its own
findings.suggestion: Acceptable given ^22.2 is pinned; if the team wants insurance against near-term churn, introduce a small typed helper (e.g. pageResource(loader)) in core/ so all six call sites share one seam

findings.issue: @Service() decorator shipped in v22.1 (~5 months old); offers no behavioral benefit over @Injectable({providedIn: 'root'}) here
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep — it is stable in v22 and the CLI default — but the revert path to @Injectable is mechanical if the team standardizes on the older form

findings.issue: resource() with no params and a loader that reads no reactive state — a stable one-shot fetch wrapped in a reloadable primitive
findings.suggestion: Harmless and idiomatic; no action needed, noted only because it is the one use where a plain promise + signal would do the same

summary: The app uses zero experimental, preview or canary APIs; it targets the current stable Angular v22.2. Its reach for newness is limited to two APIs stabilized in v22 itself — resource() as the data backbone of every page and the @Service() decorator — both confirmed stable and both well-justified by the simplification they buy. Risk is low: caret-pinned to v22 and the swap surface is six one-line declarations.
